answer: Proof-of-burn curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to provably destroy base-layer tokens to mint operational credentials. Verifying burn transactions through a cryptographic prism ensures credentials cannot be duplicated. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of burnt tokens per identity, erecting an economic ledge that stops swarms before they raven network bounties. However, this design permanently destroys capital and disadvantages resource-constrained agents.
